direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Pinned title over portraits
hero.blueprint: A pale flat ground. The title runs on one line of extra-bold uppercase at clamp(90px, 10vw, 160px), centred, spanning about 82% of the width, its cap line 120px from the top. It lives in a sticky layer (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`) stacked above the images and set in one saturated ink that reads on both ground and photograph. Beneath it a single portrait photograph, 2:3, sits centred on columns 5–8 (about 37% of the width) and runs from 90px below the top edge down to the bottom edge, so the title crosses its upper quarter and the middle letters sit on the image. The wordmark sits top-left at 24px in 15px bold; one 'Menu' word sits top-right. Bottom-left on columns 1–3: the supporting sentence as a narrow column at 16px bold, max 26ch, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. Bottom-right: the single action as a solid rectangular button. As the page scrolls, further portraits of identical ratio and position replace the first, five to eight in all, each bringing its own flat ground colour sampled from the photograph, before the layer releases.
hero.mobile: The title stays pinned at the top at 17vw on one line, or two lines at 15vw if longer than ten characters. Each portrait becomes full width minus 16px margins at 2:3 and starts behind the lower half of the title. The supporting sentence follows the first portrait at 16px. The action button is fixed to the bottom-right corner, 16px in. The wordmark shrinks to a monogram top-left.
hero.headline: The title of the series, or the name: one uppercase line of up to about 14 characters at 10vw, two short lines on a phone.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Pinned heading, passing rows
sections.blueprint: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content. Columns 1–5: the heading, two or three words, at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px) in the heaviest weight, position: sticky; top: 32px, so it holds while the right side travels. Columns 7–12: four to six capability blocks stacked with 120px between them. Each block is a title at 28px bold, then a two-part row: a portrait photograph at 3:4, 180–220px wide with square corners, and beside it, top-aligned, a plain list of four to six short lines at 18px with 14px between lines. Photographs alternate between the left and the right of their list, so the column does not read as a ladder. One ink colour, chosen for contrast on the field. The heading releases when the bottom of the last block reaches it.
sections.mobile: The heading becomes a sticky bar at the top of the section: one line at 9vw on the field colour with 12px padding, holding while blocks pass under it. Each block stacks its title, a full-width 4:3 photograph, then the list at 17px. 72px between blocks.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: One verb at a time
sections.blueprint: Three to five full-bleed panels, each 100svh tall, stacked with no gap; each is one stage and holds one photograph covering it. In every panel a single word, the verb for that stage ('Cut', 'Fold', 'Stitch', 'Press'), is set at clamp(96px, 17vw, 300px), heavy and centred, inside a wrapper that is position: sticky; top: 50% and shifted up by half its own height. Because each word is sticky only within its own panel, it holds the centre of the screen while its photograph passes behind it, and is then pushed out by the next panel's verb. Use mix-blend-mode: difference in white, or one solid colour tested on every image. One sentence at 18px sits in the bottom-left corner of each panel over a neutral scrim limited to that corner. There is no separate heading: the verbs, read in order, are both the heading and the sequence.
sections.mobile: Panels stay 100svh, each photograph cropped to a vertical slice. The verb is 24vw, still sticky at the centre. The sentence sits along the bottom over a scrim at 16px, full width with 16px margins.

sections.name: Sticky photograph, active list
sections.blueprint: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is `position: sticky; top: 12vh` and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground. The right, columns 7–11, holds a vertical list of five to nine names (treatments, rooms, courses, services) at clamp(20px, 1.6vw, 24px), each row 58px tall with the name at the left and a price or duration right-aligned at 15px in the soft ink. The active row is full ink; the others rest at 40% opacity. Hovering, focusing or scrolling a row to the middle of the viewport makes it active, crossfades the left photograph to that item's image over 300ms, and opens a three-line description at 15px, 34ch wide, directly under the name, pushing later rows down. A heading of two or three words at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px) sits above the list, aligned to its left edge, 48px above the first row.
sections.mobile: The photograph becomes a 4:3 band pinned to the top of the screen at 38svh while the list scrolls beneath it; the heading sits above the first row. Rows are 56px tall and the description opens on tap. The image changes with the row nearest the band.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: NORMAL IS BORING
references.idea: The brand name is split and half of it turned upside down: a plain sans first word top-left and a serif last word flipped 180 degrees bottom-right stay fixed while panels slide sideways between them.
references.hero: A white panel fills the left 80%; a full-height interior photo takes the right 20%. Top-left: the first word of the name in light geometric capitals, about 56px. Bottom-right of the white panel: an italic 'is' above the last word in bold didone, rotated 180 degrees so it reads upside down. Three small caps nav links run vertically up the panel's right edge. The 50px headline is broken into three two-line fragments on different columns and baselines: one at 21% from the left, one a line lower at 42%, one back at 21% whose last word turns bold italic didone. A seven-line 13px paragraph hangs beneath the middle fragment.
references.type: Izmir, a light geometric sans in capitals, for wordmark, hero fragments and 13px body; Juana, a high-contrast didone, bold italic for accent words and huge roman capitals (10-12vw and larger, cropped) for scrolling statements; Editorial New ultralight for the reversed paragraph.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #ece4da #c7d7e9 #db5c59 #1f9aa0 — White and black panels alternate with warm beige; pale blue and coral panels appear deeper in. Type stays black or white. A single teal dot acts as cursor; photos bring wood and plant tones.
references.imagery: Warm interior and garden photography of finished homes in natural light, wood and linen tones. Square-cornered; used as full-height strips, full-bleed panels and smaller insets laid over larger photos by about a third.
references.layout: Reads as a sideways journey: white, black and beige panels slide horizontally with photos and oversized words cropped by panel edges. Text fragments sit on an irregular grid; the two halves of the logo stay fixed in opposite corners.

sections.description: The photo strip from the hero grows to a full-height panel while a second, smaller interior photo slides over it, overlapping by roughly a third. To the right a white panel carries a four-line statement in didone capitals about 90px tall, set so the lines run off the panel edge and are completed only as scrolling continues. A small 12px paragraph sits under the statement's left edge.

Full black panel. A nine-line paragraph in an ultralight serif at about 32px starts 70% of the way across and runs off the right edge; its words fade from white through grey to near-black line by line as a scroll-driven reveal. A single photo of a pool at dusk, roughly 300px square, sits alone in the lower-left third. The menu pill and flipped logo invert to white.

Values panel on beige. Along the left edge a vertical ticker repeats one word in 90px didone capitals rotated 90 degrees, separated by thin eight-point asterisks. Beside it a large exterior photograph of a stone-and-glass house with a bathroom photo about half its size laid over its lower-right corner, square edges, no shadow or border.

Beige panel where the project title is set so large that single didone letters exceed the viewport height and are cropped top and bottom, acting as black shapes in the left half. In the right half a modest 300px-wide aerial photo floats with a bracketed year above and a centred serif caption and two-line descriptor below.

steal: Split a two-part brand name into opposite corners of the viewport and flip one half 180 degrees so the logo enacts the name.
Break a headline into fragments on different columns and baselines, like a stair, and hang the body paragraph under one fragment only.
Scale a project title until single letters are taller than the viewport, then float a small captioned photo beside those cropped shapes.
references.media: The only picture on the first screen is an interior photograph cropped to the right 20% (290px, full height), the leading edge of a pinned horizontal track that widens to about 65% on the next screen. Inside the track, overlapping pairs lay a smaller photograph over a larger full-height one, project cards widen as they reach the centre, and a photograph sits framed in a flat coral field; all 29 images have square corners and reveal by clip-path while scaling down from 1.5, and there is no video.
references.motion: About 2.5s of entrance: the logo, then headline characters, then body lines rising from masks (y over 0.65-0.97s power3.out at a 0.025-0.033 stagger), then the photo and nav. One section pins for +=1150% (about 10,350px) at scrub 1 and is translated sideways; photo pairs move on scrub 0.35, a statement fills line by line on scrub 0, and project cards widen over 1s power1.inOut; a dot cursor grows with a back-out overshoot the house layer does not use.

references.name: Revelatio Studio
references.idea: The team photograph is the hero: it starts as a small CRT-curved mosaic of typographic glyphs and resolves into a full-bleed group portrait as you scroll.
references.hero: Pure black viewport. Centred, about 58% of the width and 57% of the height, is a canvas showing a group photo rebuilt from tiny coloured glyphs, its edges barrel-distorted like a CRT tube; it is dim, so black dominates. The headline is modest: two lines at 2.5vw in regular-weight grotesk, flush to the bottom-left corner with a 30px margin. Navigation is split into two small dark-grey rounded rectangles: logo mark plus four links top-left, language switch and contact top-right. Nothing else; roughly 80% of the screen is black.
references.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman is the only face and weight. Headline just 36px with -0.03em tracking against 15px body; hierarchy comes from position and grey value. The footer city list jumps to roughly 5vw; the digest records a 12.5vw maximum.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #2b2b2b #8a8a8a — Black intro and footer, white work and capabilities sections. The interface has no accent; all colour comes from project thumbnails and the faint tints inside the glyph mosaic.
references.imagery: A studio group portrait rendered as a glyph mosaic on canvas, then as a dim near-full-bleed photograph; project tiles are square-cornered brand visuals in saturated flat colours, set on white with caption rows beneath.
references.layout: About 30px side margins throughout. Black full-screen opening, then a white work grid mixing one large tile with a narrow companion and a three-up row, a three-column plain-text capabilities list, and a black footer of oversized dim text. Captions sit under images, tags right-aligned.

sections.description: Pinned for about two viewports: the hero canvas grows with scroll from a centred 58%-wide mosaic to a near full-bleed image with a thin black margin, while the glyph cells shrink until the picture reads as a dim photograph of about twenty people. The headline scrolls away and only the two nav boxes remain in the top corners.

White background. First row: one large landscape tile spanning roughly two-thirds of the width beside a narrower tile about one-third wide and half as tall, top-aligned. Second row: three equal tiles. All square-cornered with about 16px gutters. Beneath each: project name at left, two tiny grey tags right-aligned on the same line, then a two-line grey description at about 11px. A small underlined see-all link with an arrow sits below the grid at left.

White section opened by a hairline and a tiny label. Three text columns, each with a small grey category title and beneath it a tight stack of eight to ten service names in 15px regular grotesk at about 1.2 line-height, with no bullets, icons or cards. Columns share the work grid's left edges, leaving the right third partly empty.

Black full-viewport block filled with a run-on, comma-separated list of client cities set at about 5vw in very dark grey, barely visible against black, wrapping over seven flush-left lines. Exactly one city, the last, is lit white, which implies a cycling highlight. The nav boxes stay fixed at the top corners.

steal: Render a photograph as a grid of small coloured glyphs on canvas and let scroll increase its size and resolution until it becomes the real photo.
Hold the hero headline at 2.5vw in a bottom corner and let a dim central image and empty black carry the scale.
Set a long list in near-invisible dark grey at display size and light one item at a time.
references.media: A centred 16:10 canvas covering 60% of the width and height plays the team film as a dot matrix with a curved, tube-like outline, and grows to cover the whole screen over three screens of scroll. Below: an asymmetric two-plus-one then three-up grid of 16:9 work cards (video players scaled to 133% of the card so the letterboxing is cropped), a cursor image trail over a pinned city list, a draggable marquee of result cards, and a slider of cards with staggered image heights bleeding off the right edge; square corners.
references.motion: No preloader was seen and the hero is composed at 400ms (load 23s); Lenis then holds two sticky 900px stages, the hero screen scaling from 60% to full bleed over 2700px and one city at a time lighting up over 3600px. The ground flips black, white, black by section with a 0.35s ease on colour across about 11,000 nodes, stat numerals roll like an odometer, and transforms run 0.4s on cubic-bezier(0.625,0.05,0,1) with 0.8s exits on (0.625,0,0.875,0).

references.name: /zeroz Brand Site
references.idea: A single supplement pouch floats in a green-lit 3D room, and bursts of white light act as the scene changes between short statements.
references.hero: The captured first viewport is a white light bloom mid-transition; the settled hero appears one frame later. A dark green 3D room with a hexagonal ceiling lamp fills the screen. A green pouch, about 35% of viewport height, floats tilted at dead centre with a white tablet beside it. The headline is split around it: two centred lines above and two below at 5.6vw in regular Helvetica Now, partly overlapping the pouch. Large thin parentheses bracket the product, and tiny three-line labels sit far left and far right at the same height. Wordmark top-left, four links top-centre, a small white store tab pinned top-right, a Japanese tagline bottom-centre.
references.type: HelveticaNowDisplay Regular for Latin headlines at 80px, centred, no tracking; Tazugane Gothic Regular and Medium for Japanese at about 18px with wide letter-spacing. Regular weights only, so scale and white-on-green contrast do the work. The footer wordmark is custom slashed lettering spanning the full width.
references.colour: #1f3a26 #00a852 #ffffff #455a48 #111312 — Everything is one green: dark and smoky in the 3D room, saturated flat green in the footer and store tab. White appears as light itself, blooming to fill the screen between scenes.
references.imagery: Real-time 3D pouch and tablet in a fogged green room with a hexagonal spotlight and floor glow; full-bleed canvas, no photographs visible, soft volumetric light and heavy lens bloom.
references.layout: A pinned full-screen canvas driven by nearly fifty screens of scroll; text arrives as short centred statements inside discs of white light. Slim fixed nav. Only the footer becomes a flat layout, with a logo left, a link column near centre and a giant wordmark.

sections.description: The room stays in place while a soft-edged white disc, about 45% of viewport width with a wide feathered falloff, opens at centre where the product hung. Inside it sits a three-line centred statement in dark grey: wide-tracked Japanese on lines one and three, a quoted Latin phrase in light grotesk on line two, all around 18 to 20px. The green floor glow and ceiling lamp remain visible around the disc.

Between scenes the pouch dissolves into a ball of light at centre: thin radial streak lines fly outward, the hexagonal lamp flares overhead, and the tablet remains as the only solid object, drifting to the lower right of the glow. The nav wordmark and store tab switch from white to green as the background brightens.

Flat saturated green block one viewport tall. Parent-company logo top-left in white, a five-item link column starting just right of centre, an underlined store link top-right. The bottom half is the wordmark with its leading slash, in white, scaled to run from the left edge to the right edge at about 28% of viewport height. A single line of legal links sits beneath it at 10px.

steal: Split a four-line headline into two lines above and two below a centred product, letting the object interrupt the sentence.
Use a feathered disc of white light as the text container instead of a card.
End the page on a flat field of the brand colour with the wordmark scaled edge to edge.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers the fold and renders the whole story: a dark green room in one-point perspective with a glowing ceiling panel, a tilted pouch and tablet at about 23% of the width bracketed by the split headline, a light disc that becomes the text page, a burst of the logo and photographs, and about 20 lifestyle photos as skewed cards on a 3D ribbon round a chapter title. DOM video appears only in the closing link index, eight short loops stacked on portrait pictures.
references.motion: A light burst comes first (the page took 19.5s to load), then the product with its headline by 2.5s and the nav by 4.5s, and Lenis then drives the fixed canvas through long sticky runways (10,152px for the opening): the camera dollies into the ceiling light, the manifesto advances one line at a time in a reading spotlight, and the photo ribbon arcs over the top as the ground goes from dark green to white to mint. The house ease is cubic-bezier(.3,.26,.38,1), 67 uses, mostly at 0.3-0.5s, and staggered rises step by 40ms per index.
